chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn al-'Arzami, from Hatim ibn Isma'il al-Madini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that

the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to drink water while standing, then drank from the remainder of his ablution water while standing. Then he turned toward al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'O my son! I saw your grandfather, the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), do like this.'

key_terms.صَنَعَ هَكَذَا: 'Did like this' — a demonstrative affirmation linking the Imam's action to prophetic practice
key_terms.فَضْلُ الْوَضُوء: The leftover/remainder of wudu water — the water remaining after completing ablution, considered blessed
key_terms.قَائِم: Standing upright; the posture described here contrasts with the general preference for sitting when drinking in some traditions

ai.seo_question: Is drinking water while standing permissible in Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates that Imam Ali (AS) would drink water while standing and also consume the leftover water from his wudu while standing. He then turned to his son al-Husayn (AS) and explained that he had witnessed the Prophet (SAWW) perform these same actions. This hadith establishes the permissibility of drinking water while standing and the virtue of consuming leftover ablution water in that posture, grounded in explicit prophetic precedent.
